note: P4.D169 item 5 — the side-effect applier's corpus, 49 rows. Rows 1-15 are v4's `__tests__/unit/lib/pascal/side-effects.test.ts` (the state/metadata matrix that predates progressions, so the family is green on the pre-change applier); rows 16-47 are its `side-effects-progress.test.ts` siblings. v4 has 31 `it`s there and this has 32 rows, which is four deliberate departures: its increment case asserts twice and became two rows, its declined-time case loops three values and became three, its `warns naming the character's progression and the issue` is the SAME input as the drop-and-restore row above it and rides that row's `warns` comparand rather than repeating the input, and its `defaults nowMs to the wall clock` has no row at all — v5's `now_ms` is not optional (the entrance passes the reading it already took), which is a recorded divergence, not a gap. v4's three commit-half fail-soft cases have no row either: they mock a repository REJECTION, which the pure planning pass this corpus drives cannot express — v5 proves those in `side_effects.rs`'s commit tests.
